missing_or_uncertain: Exact timing of onset after restart (not specified) but rechallenge pattern strongly supports drug causality

F06: rash resolved after drug discontinuation and corticosteroids
F10: marked leukocytosis, hyperglycemia, hypoproteinemia, transaminitis, elevated CRP
F11: skin biopsy: subcorneal collections of neutrophils
F12: skin biopsy: spongiotic epidermis with neutrophilic exocytosis

candidates.label: Acute generalized pustular psoriasis (von Zumbusch type)

response.rationale: The temporal recurrence after hydroxychloroquine rechallenge (2022) with prior resolution on discontinuation (2010) is a hallmark of drug-induced AGEP. Cutaneous findings of widespread erythema, desquamation, pustulation, systemic laboratory abnormalities (leukocytosis, transaminitis, elevated CRP), and biopsy showing subcorneal neutrophilic pustules with spongiotic epidermis and neutrophilic exocytosis all strongly support AGEP. The denial of psoriasis and the drug-specific pattern distinguish it from pustular psoriasis. Other differentials like Sneddon-Wilkinson, Sweet syndrome, or pemphigus are less compatible with the biopsy and systemic presentation. The high margin is based on the definitive rechallenge data and classic histology.
